audit_title: HoneyChain SIH'26 Full-System Error & Vulnerability Forensic Audit

findings.description: Unauthenticated public POST endpoint /api/v1/health/clean truncates all core database tables via CASCADE without any authentication, role check, or CSRF protection.
findings.root_cause: A development test fixture cleanup endpoint was mounted directly to the main Express router in server/index.js without environment guards (e.g. checking process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') or authentication middleware.
findings.evidence: app.post('/api/v1/health/clean', async (req, res) => { const tables = ['alerts', 'notifications', 'certificates', 'quality_results', 'test_requests', 'inspections', 'provenance_events', 'batch_relationships', 'batches', 'hives', 'pending_applications']; await pool.query(`TRUNCATE TABLE ${tables.join(', ')} CASCADE;`); res.json({ status: 'ok', message: 'All operational data truncated successfully.' }); });
findings.reproduction: Execute: curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/v1/health/clean without any cookies, headers, or tokens. The server responds with HTTP 200 and all database records are permanently deleted.
findings.impact: Complete data destruction by any anonymous user, bot, or automated security scanner with network access to the API.
findings.recommendation: Immediately remove this endpoint from production builds, or strictly gate it behind process.env.NODE_ENV === 'test' with admin API key validation.
findings.regression_test: tests/security.test.js: Send unauthenticated POST /api/v1/health/clean; assert HTTP 404 or 401.

findings.description: Production database connection strings containing plaintext usernames, passwords, and hosts for both Neon Serverless PostgreSQL and MongoDB Atlas are committed directly to version control.
findings.root_cause: The active server/.env file was checked into git instead of being restricted to .gitignore, exposing production database credentials.
findings.evidence: server/.env lines 7 & 20: DATABASE_URL=postgresql://neondb_owner:npg_JBhe4bwDVp3c@ep-broad-pine-a50y80ut-pooler.us-east-2.aws.neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require and MONGODB_URI=mongodb+srv://esp32_user:honeychain2026@esp32cluster.w7u0bdo.mongodb.net/?appName=ESP32Cluster
findings.reproduction: Inspect server/.env in any git checkout. The credentials allow direct connection to both PostgreSQL and MongoDB Atlas clusters using standard CLI tools.
findings.impact: Full database compromise, arbitrary data exfiltration, tampering with provenance and batch logs, and unauthorized compute charges on cloud database accounts.
findings.recommendation: Immediately rotate credentials on Neon Console and MongoDB Atlas. Remove server/.env from git history using git filter-repo or BFG Repo-Cleaner, and enforce git secret scanning in CI.
findings.regression_test: CI secret scan using git-secrets or TruffleHog to detect high-entropy keys and connection strings.

findings.description: POST /api/v1/batches allows any authenticated user to create a honey batch under any producer's identity by supplying an arbitrary producerId in the request body.
findings.root_cause: The handler prioritizes req.body.producerId over the authenticated token: const effectiveProducerId = producerId || req.user.multiActorIds?.beekeeper || req.user.actorId without checking if req.user has admin privileges.
findings.evidence: server/routes/batchRoutes.js:92: const effectiveProducerId = producerId || req.user.multiActorIds?.beekeeper || req.user.actorId;
findings.reproduction: Authenticate as user 'BK-001' and send POST /api/v1/batches with JSON body containing 'producerId': 'BK-999'. The batch is successfully inserted with producer_id = 'BK-999'.
findings.impact: Beekeepers can fabricate harvest batches in the name of competing apiaries, corrupting traceability attribution and regulatory auditing.
findings.recommendation: Enforce that non-admin callers can only create batches where effectiveProducerId is strictly bound to req.user.actorId or their verified role alias.
findings.regression_test: tests/security.test.js: Authenticate as BK-001, POST /batches with producerId: BK-999; assert HTTP 403 Forbidden.

findings.description: POST /api/v1/hives permits any authenticated user to register apiary hives under another beekeeper's account without administrative authorization.
findings.root_cause: The handler trusts req.body.producerId without verifying whether the caller is authorized to register assets on behalf of another user: const assignedProducer = producerId || req.user.multiActorIds?.beekeeper || req.user.actorId;
findings.evidence: server/routes/hiveRoutes.js:87: const assignedProducer = producerId || req.user.multiActorIds?.beekeeper || req.user.actorId;
findings.reproduction: Authenticate as BK-001, POST /hives with { hiveId: 'H-ILLEGAL', producerId: 'BK-045' }. The hive is inserted and owned by BK-045.
findings.impact: Attackers can register fraudulent hives or pollute victim beekeepers' monitoring dashboards with rogue sensor associations.
findings.recommendation: Restrict producerId override strictly to users holding the 'kvic' or 'admin' role. All standard beekeepers must be pinned to req.user.actorId.
findings.regression_test: tests/security.test.js: Non-admin POST /hives with foreign producerId; assert HTTP 403 Forbidden.

findings.description: PATCH /api/v1/batches/:batchId allows arbitrary modification of lifecycle stage, quantity, processing method, and certificate references with zero state machine validation.
findings.root_cause: The backend PATCH route only checks if the caller is the producer or assigned processor, but does not enforce stage ordering, positive quantity checks, or transition prerequisites.
findings.evidence: server/routes/batchRoutes.js:166-176 dynamically pushes any supplied stage, quantity, certificateId, and certStatus into the SQL UPDATE statement.
findings.reproduction: Authenticate as the owner of a Stage 6 (Certified) batch. Send PATCH /api/v1/batches/:id with { stage: 1, quantity: 99999, certStatus: 'PENDING' }. The update succeeds, regressing the certified batch to Stage 1.
findings.impact: Completely breaks the integrity of the honey supply chain. Any beekeeper or processor can alter harvest volumes after inspection or reverse processing stages.
findings.recommendation: Implement a strict state machine validator on the backend that rejects backward transitions, forbids quantity changes once processing starts, and requires specific roles for stage advancements.
findings.regression_test: tests/security.test.js: PATCH a Stage 6 batch to stage 1; assert HTTP 400 or 409 Conflict.

findings.description: POST /api/v1/lab/certificates only requires authentication but lacks role authorization. Any logged-in user can issue official AGMARK certificates.
findings.root_cause: The router applies requireAuth instead of requireRole('laboratory', 'verifier', 'kvic', 'admin').
findings.evidence: server/routes/labRoutes.js:218: router.post('/certificates', requireAuth, async (req, res, next) => { ... });
findings.reproduction: Log in as a beekeeper or retailer account. Send POST /api/v1/lab/certificates with a valid batchId. An AGMARK certificate is generated and the batch is marked CERTIFIED.
findings.impact: Unauthorized actors can self-certify adulterated or uninspected honey batches, completely undermining the regulatory value of the platform.
findings.recommendation: Add requireRole('laboratory', 'verifier', 'kvic', 'admin') to POST /api/v1/lab/certificates and POST /api/v1/lab/quality-results.
findings.regression_test: tests/security.test.js: Authenticate as beekeeper, POST /lab/certificates; assert HTTP 403 Forbidden.

findings.description: Real-time Server-Sent Events (SSE) telemetry stream /api/v1/sensors/stream and endpoints /latest and /history have no authentication or access control.
findings.root_cause: The sensor router mounts GET /stream, GET /latest, and GET /history without any authentication middleware, and sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.
findings.evidence: server/routes/sensorRoutes.js:214: router.get('/stream', async (req, res) => { ... Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * ... });
findings.reproduction: Open a browser or curl http://localhost:3001/api/v1/sensors/stream without any cookies or headers. The connection opens and streams live apiary sensor data in real-time.
findings.impact: Competitors or attackers can eavesdrop on private apiary environmental data, hive locations, temperature fluctuations, and theft vibration alerts.
findings.recommendation: Add authenticateRequest or requireAuth to all telemetry reading endpoints, and filter streaming events by authorized hive ownership.
findings.regression_test: tests/sensor.test.js: GET /sensors/stream without auth; assert HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

findings.description: The application UI displays trust claims such as 'Provenance Status', 'Trust Seal', and 'Cryptographic Ledger Trail', but no blockchain integration exists.
findings.root_cause: blockchainService.js is an explicit mock seam returning BLOCKCHAIN_NOT_CONNECTED, while UI components display simulated cryptographic cards and readiness scores.
findings.evidence: blockchainService.js:25: blockchainStatus: 'NOT_CONNECTED'. BlockchainProofCard.jsx:42: 'Event {event.eventId} is recorded in HoneyChain.'
findings.reproduction: Navigate to /app/traceability or /verify/BEE-2026-001. Expand verification details; all hashes and transaction IDs display 'Not available' while trust seals indicate verified provenance.
findings.impact: Misleads users, evaluators, and jury members regarding actual blockchain immutability and cryptographic guarantees.
findings.recommendation: Clearly label all provenance records as 'Local Relational Audit Log (Blockchain Gateway Not Connected)', and replace mock scores with honest architecture status.
findings.regression_test: tests/remediation.test.js: Verify prepareEvent returns NOT_CONNECTED and UI truthfulness badges remain uninflated.

findings.description: The 'AI Honey Frame Inspection' feature simulates Varroa mite and brood disease detection using a deterministic string hash modulo formula rather than an ML/CV model.
findings.root_cause: runAiHealthAnalysis computes a hash of hiveId + fileName + fileSize and returns hardcoded diagnosis strings with fake confidence percentages (e.g. 93.4%).
findings.evidence: hiveService.js:65: const seed = hashString(`${hiveId}-${fileName}-${fileSize}`); const isHighRisk = (seed % 10) >= 7 || hiveId === 'H-1030'; confidence: +(88.5 + (seed % 80) / 10).toFixed(1)
findings.reproduction: Upload any arbitrary JPEG image (e.g. a blank square) named test.jpg. The UI displays 'Varroa Destructor Mite Infestation Detected (91.2% confidence)' based solely on filename characters.
findings.impact: Severe product truthfulness violation. Beekeepers relying on the demo could misdiagnose hive health, and jury members will identify it as fake AI.
findings.recommendation: Prominently display a 'Simulation / Prototype Demonstration' badge on the AI inspection UI, and integrate a real TensorFlow.js or cloud-hosted ONNX model seam.
findings.regression_test: tests/remediation.test.js: AI health analysis output must contain explicit isSimulated: true flag.

findings.description: QRCodeCard encodes a hardcoded URL to https://beecrypt.demo/verify/:batchId, which fails DNS resolution when scanned by real mobile devices.
findings.root_cause: The component hardcodes the domain string 'https://beecrypt.demo/verify/' instead of resolving window.location.origin or an environment variable VITE_PUBLIC_URL.
findings.evidence: src/components/QRCodeCard.jsx:10: const url = `https://beecrypt.demo/verify/${batchId}`;
findings.reproduction: Display a QR code on the Retailer Inventory or Extraction page and scan it with a physical mobile camera. The phone browser fails with NXDOMAIN (server not found).
findings.impact: Completely breaks the core live consumer verification demonstration at SIH.
findings.recommendation: Dynamically generate the QR URL using window.location.origin (for web) or import.meta.env.VITE_PUBLIC_VERIFY_URL with fallback.
findings.regression_test: Scan test / mock URL verification in QRCodeCard component test.

findings.description: Capacitor Android configuration disables cleartext HTTP traffic while AndroidManifest.xml omits android:usesCleartextTraffic, causing all local LAN/IoT HTTP requests to fail on Android.
findings.root_cause: capacitor.config.json sets 'cleartext': false, and Android 9+ enforces HTTPS by default. The local backend (http://10.131.229.86:3001) and ESP32 camera (http://10.131.229.39) use cleartext HTTP.
findings.evidence: capacitor.config.json:8: 'cleartext': false. AndroidManifest.xml lines 5-11 do not include android:usesCleartextTraffic='true'.
findings.reproduction: Build and run the Android APK on a physical phone on the local Wi-Fi. All API and camera calls fail with ERR_CLEARTEXT_NOT_PERMITTED.
findings.impact: The compiled Android mobile application cannot communicate with either the backend API or IoT hardware.
findings.recommendation: Set cleartext: true in capacitor.config.json for dev builds, or configure a network_security_config.xml permitting local LAN IPs, or deploy backend behind valid HTTPS.
findings.regression_test: Inspect compiled Android manifest and capacitor configuration for network policy compliance.

findings.description: CI quality gate pipeline intentionally masks test suite failures using an echo fallback, allowing broken code to pass CI and build release APKs.
findings.root_cause: Line 34 appends || echo to the test command: npm test || echo 'Test suite completed with cloud network notice. Continuing to build...'.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:34: run: npm test || echo 'Test suite completed with cloud network notice. Continuing to build...'
findings.reproduction: Introduce an intentional assertion failure in any test file and push to a branch. The GitHub Action step reports green/success despite test failures.
findings.impact: Breaks the continuous integration feedback loop, permitting broken code and critical security regressions into release artifacts.
findings.recommendation: Remove the echo fallback. Mock all cloud network dependencies in unit tests so that npm test runs hermetically and fails reliably on assertion errors.
findings.regression_test: CI pipeline must exit with non-zero code on test failure.

findings.description: If the backend API is unreachable or returns a non-401 error, login silently falls back to client-side in-memory DEMO_USERS, creating phantom local sessions.
findings.root_cause: The catch block logs a warning and falls back to DEMO_USERS[normalizedEmail], ignoring password verification.
findings.evidence: src/services/authService.js:21-25: console.warn('Backend API login unreachable, falling back to mock:', err.message); const mockUser = DEMO_USERS[normalizedEmail]; return mockUser;
findings.reproduction: Stop the backend server. Enter beekeeper@beecrypt.demo with an arbitrary password 'wrongpassword123'. The frontend logs in successfully into an unpersisted session.
findings.impact: Creates a misleading demo state where mutations are written to localStorage only, and fail silently when attempting to sync with PostgreSQL.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly notify the user with an offline warning dialog, and prevent mock logins unless an explicit DEMO_MODE toggle is enabled.
findings.regression_test: tests/remediation.test.js: Test login failure propagates error when backend is disconnected.

findings.description: verifyOtp accepts any arbitrary 6-digit sequence without checking against a stored OTP, and loginWithGoogle is an 800ms fake timeout returning the beekeeper account.
findings.root_cause: verifyOtp only checks if otp.length === 6. Google OAuth does not use Google Identity Services SDK or exchange an OAuth token with the backend.
findings.evidence: src/services/authService.js:91: if (otp.length === 6) resolve({ verified: true }). Lines 37-48 resolve beekeeper@beecrypt.demo regardless of Google account.
findings.reproduction: Navigate to /verify-otp and enter 000000. Verification succeeds. Click 'Continue with Google'; user is logged in as BK-001 without opening Google OAuth popup.
findings.impact: Exposes incomplete authentication features to the jury, highlighting mock implementations rather than production capabilities.
findings.recommendation: Either integrate real Google OAuth and SMS/email OTP via Twilio/SendGrid, or clearly label recovery workflows as 'Demonstration Simulation'.
findings.regression_test: Unit tests for OTP length vs content validation.

findings.description: No Dockerfile or docker-compose.yml configuration exists in the entire repository, preventing reproducible containerized deployment.
findings.root_cause: The project relies entirely on host-installed Node.js, external cloud databases, and manual background process execution.
findings.evidence: File search for Dockerfile and *compose* returns zero results in the entire workspace.
findings.reproduction: Attempt to run docker build or docker compose up in the project directory; command fails with file not found.
findings.impact: High risk of environment configuration drift, missing system dependencies, and deployment failure on staging or production servers.
findings.recommendation: Create a multi-stage Dockerfile for the frontend (Nginx) and backend (Node.js Alpine), along with a docker-compose.yml providing local PostgreSQL and MongoDB containers.
findings.regression_test: Execute docker compose build and verify all containers build and pass health checks.

findings.description: resetAllData calls a hardcoded localhost URL http://localhost:3001/api/v1/health/clean, which fails on mobile devices and wipes all database tables when clicked.
findings.root_cause: resetAllData bypasses the dynamic apiClient helper and directly invokes fetch('http://localhost:3001/api/v1/health/clean', { method: 'POST' }).
findings.evidence: src/context/AppContext.jsx:208: await fetch('http://localhost:3001/api/v1/health/clean', { method: 'POST' });
findings.reproduction: On mobile or remote desktop, trigger the data reset action in the UI. A network error occurs or it wipes the shared cloud PostgreSQL database.
findings.impact: Dual failure: hardcoded localhost fails on phones, and successful execution wipes the entire database.
findings.recommendation: Remove this call from the UI, and scope local reset to localStorage only.
findings.regression_test: Search for hardcoded localhost URLs across src/ directory.

findings.description: GET /api/v1/events requires authentication, preventing anonymous consumers who scan a honey jar QR code from querying the batch provenance trail.
findings.root_cause: router.get('/', requireAuth, ...) applies the requireAuth middleware to the entire events list endpoint without providing a public read-only query by batchId.
findings.evidence: server/routes/eventRoutes.js:27: router.get('/', requireAuth, async (req, res, next) => { ... });
findings.reproduction: Attempt to fetch http://localhost:3001/api/v1/events?batchId=BEE-2026-001 without an Authorization header or cookie. The server returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated consumers scanning product packaging cannot see the provenance timeline from the backend API, forcing the frontend to rely on stale mock events.
findings.recommendation: Allow unauthenticated GET requests when a specific batchId query parameter is provided (e.g. GET /api/v1/events/public?batchId=...).
findings.regression_test: tests/security.test.js: Anonymous GET /events?batchId=... returns public event records.

findings.description: Private local network IP address 10.131.229.86 is hardcoded in both the Arduino firmware source and the frontend mobile API fallback.
findings.root_cause: The developer's laptop Wi-Fi DHCP address was hardcoded during physical testing instead of using DNS hostnames, mDNS, or configurable EEPROM/WiFiManager.
findings.evidence: firmware/ESP32_Telemetry.ino:44: const char* BACKEND_URL = 'http://10.131.229.86:3001/api/v1/sensors/telemetry'; src/config/env.js:55: return 'http://10.131.229.86:3001/api/v1';
findings.reproduction: Connect the ESP32 or mobile app to a different Wi-Fi network (e.g. SIH venue Wi-Fi). Transmission fails immediately because the IP 10.131.229.86 is unreachable.
findings.impact: Immediate failure during live hackathon evaluation when switching network environments.
findings.recommendation: Use WiFiManager or Captive Portal on the ESP32 to configure backend endpoints over Wi-Fi, and configure mobile API URLs via .env build flags.
findings.regression_test: Search codebase for hardcoded private subnet IP literals.

findings.description: Sensor firmware transmits telemetry every 3,000 ms over unencrypted HTTP without deep sleep, local buffering, or exponential backoff.
findings.root_cause: SEND_INTERVAL_MS = 3000 in continuous loop mode causes high battery consumption and floods the database with ~28,800 records/day per hive.
findings.evidence: firmware/ESP32_Telemetry.ino:54: const unsigned long SEND_INTERVAL_MS = 3000; and Snprintf payload sent via HTTPClient with no deep sleep.
findings.reproduction: Flash the firmware to ESP32. Observe 20 HTTP POST requests per minute in backend logs. Power consumption remains at ~160mA continuously.
findings.impact: Apiary field nodes powered by battery/solar will deplete within 24–48 hours; network interruptions cause immediate data loss with no local storage.
findings.recommendation: Implement ESP32 deep sleep cycles (e.g. 5–15 minute wake intervals), batch readings, and store unsent samples in SPIFFS/LittleFS flash during Wi-Fi outages.
findings.regression_test: Verify firmware power profiling and offline flash buffer logic.

findings.description: Dependencies contain 6 vulnerabilities in frontend (including critical hardlink path traversal in tar) and 3 moderate vulnerabilities in backend (qs DoS / array-limit bypass).
findings.root_cause: Transitive dependencies in @capacitor/cli (using tar <=7.5.20) and express / body-parser (using qs 2.2.5 - 6.15.3) have known CVE advisories.
findings.evidence: npm audit reports: GHSA-34x7-hfp2-rc4v (tar critical), GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx (qs moderate), GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99 (esbuild moderate).
findings.reproduction: Run npm audit in project root and server/ directory. Both report vulnerable packages.
findings.impact: Potential development machine compromise via malicious archives and server denial-of-service via crafted JSON/URL-encoded query payloads.
findings.recommendation: Update @capacitor/cli and express/body-parser to patched versions; run npm audit fix.
findings.regression_test: Execute npm audit and assert zero critical or high vulnerabilities.

findings.description: Measurement unit inconsistency: HoneyExtraction and Retailer Inventory display batch volume in kilograms (kg), while Processing.jsx displays Liters (L).
findings.root_cause: The database schema defines quantity NUMERIC(10,2) without a unit column. Different workspace views assume different physical units.
findings.evidence: Processing.jsx:94: {batch.quantity} L vs HoneyExtraction.jsx and RetailerInventory: Stock: {b.quantity} kg.
findings.reproduction: Harvest 10.0 kg of honey. Open the Processing page for the same batch; the batch header now displays 10.0 L.
findings.impact: Creates confusion for processors and retail managers, as honey density is ~1.42 kg/L, meaning 10 kg does not equal 10 Liters.
findings.recommendation: Add a unit column (e.g. 'kg' | 'L') to the batches table or standardize on kilograms across all UI dashboards.
findings.regression_test: Check unit consistency across all workspace screens for batch records.

findings.description: Key relational columns (producer_id, processor_id, lab_id, inspections.hive_id) lack foreign key constraints referencing users(actor_id) or hives(hive_id).
findings.root_cause: Table creation scripts defined these fields as bare TEXT columns rather than FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES constraints.
findings.evidence: 003_create_batches.sql lines 5, 13, 16: producer_id TEXT NOT NULL, processor_id TEXT, lab_id TEXT without REFERENCES users(actor_id).
findings.reproduction: Execute SQL: INSERT INTO batches (batch_id, producer_id) VALUES ('BEE-ORPHAN', 'NON_EXISTENT_USER'); The insert succeeds without constraint error.
findings.impact: Allows orphaned batches, inspections referencing deleted hives, and impossible supply-chain actor assignments.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit foreign key constraints with ON DELETE RESTRICT/SET NULL in a new migration.
findings.regression_test: Attempt to insert batch with invalid producer_id; assert constraint violation.

findings.description: Frontend production JavaScript bundle generates chunks exceeding Vite's 500 kB warning threshold (e.g. generateCategoricalChart 375 kB, vendor index 336 kB).
findings.root_cause: Recharts, Lucide, and React Router are bundled without manual chunk splitting or dynamic import boundaries in vite.config.js.
findings.evidence: Vite build output: dist/assets/generateCategoricalChart-B2VSEXhG.js 375.07 kB, dist/assets/index-DlXseupH.js 336.52 kB.
findings.reproduction: Run npm run build. Vite outputs warnings regarding chunk size exceeding 500 kB after minification.
findings.impact: Slower initial load times, especially on mobile 3G/4G connections and low-spec Android devices in rural apiary settings.
findings.recommendation: Configure build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks in vite.config.js to split large vendor libraries (recharts, lucide) into dedicated cached chunks.
findings.regression_test: npm run build output must produce chunks under 300 kB.

findings.description: Laboratory certificates generate synthetic file names (e.g. AGMARK-2026-XXXX.pdf) and set uploaded = true, but no actual PDF document is generated or stored.
findings.root_cause: The certificate endpoint saves metadata but does not integrate PDF generation (PDFKit/Puppeteer) or object storage (GridFS / S3 / Neon Object Storage).
findings.evidence: server/routes/labRoutes.js:247: fileName || `${effectiveId}.pdf`, uploaded: true, but no file is written to disk or database.
findings.reproduction: View a certificate in the Laboratory dashboard and click download/view; the file cannot be downloaded because no binary PDF exists.
findings.impact: Retailers and consumers cannot review actual signed lab test reports, diminishing credibility during regulatory audits.
findings.recommendation: Integrate PDF generation or allow labs to upload authentic signed test report PDFs into MongoDB GridFS or cloud object storage.
findings.regression_test: Verify certificate record has a valid resolvable file URL.

findings.description: Any authenticated user can view, list, and stream camera captures from any hive in the system without ownership verification.
findings.root_cause: GET /captures/:captureId/image and GET /captures authenticate the user's token but do not check if the capture's hiveId belongs to req.user.actorId.
findings.evidence: server/routes/cameraRoutes.js:334: authenticateRequest validates JWT, but no hive ownership query is executed before streaming imageBuffer.
findings.reproduction: Authenticate as Beekeeper A (BK-001). Request the image for a capture belonging to Beekeeper B (BK-045). The private hive photo is returned.
findings.impact: Breaches apiary privacy, enabling rival beekeepers to inspect competitor hive setups and colony health status.
findings.recommendation: Query the hives table to verify hive_id ownership against req.user.actorId before serving image streams (allowing kvic/admin override).
findings.regression_test: tests/camera.test.js: Authenticate as BK-001, request BK-045 capture image; assert HTTP 403 Forbidden.

findings.description: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) risk: The backend dispatches outbound HTTP requests to ESP32_IP without IP range validation or strict intranet isolation.
findings.root_cause: fetchFromEsp32 appends pathnames to process.env.ESP32_IP. If misconfigured or poisoned, the server could be coerced into probing internal cloud metadata endpoints.
findings.evidence: server/routes/cameraRoutes.js:131: const url = `${esp32Base}${pathname}`; const response = await fetch(url, ...);
findings.reproduction: Set ESP32_IP=http://169.254.169.254. Trigger GET /api/v1/camera/status; the server attempts an outbound request to the AWS metadata service.
findings.impact: Potential cloud credential extraction if hosted on AWS/GCP without metadata protections.
findings.recommendation: Validate that ESP32_IP conforms strictly to private RFC1918 IPv4 ranges and forbid cloud metadata IPs (169.254.x.x).
findings.regression_test: Reject non-private or cloud metadata IPs in ESP32 configuration.

findings.description: Inconsistent JWT_SECRET resolution logic between auth middleware and cameraRoutes.js.
findings.root_cause: auth.js implements resolveJwtSecret with production hard-fail guards, while cameraRoutes.js line 16 defines its own fallback: const JWT_SECRET = process.env.JWT_SECRET || 'beecrypt_dev_only_secret_DO_NOT_USE_IN_PRODUCTION';
findings.evidence: cameraRoutes.js:16 does not use resolveJwtSecret() exported from auth.js, bypassing production startup validation.
findings.reproduction: Start server with empty JWT_SECRET in production mode; auth.js throws an error, but cameraRoutes.js silently defaults to the insecure key.
findings.impact: Architectural inconsistency and risk of token verification discrepancies if secret keys differ.
findings.recommendation: Export and reuse a single centralized JWT_SECRET constant or verification function across all routes.
findings.regression_test: Ensure all route files import JWT validation from a single centralized module.

findings.description: Missing static linting (ESLint) and TypeScript type-checking scripts in package.json.
findings.root_cause: package.json scripts only define dev, build, test, and preview. No eslint or tsc --noEmit script is configured in devDependencies.
findings.evidence: package.json lines 7-21 contain no 'lint' script.
findings.reproduction: Attempt to run npm run lint; npm reports missing script.
findings.impact: Code style regressions, unused variables, and subtle type bugs can slip through into commits unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Add ESLint and TypeScript (for JSDoc type checking) to devDependencies and wire npm run lint into CI.
findings.regression_test: npm run lint executes in CI quality gate.

findings.description: Verification details toggle button lacks aria-expanded and aria-controls attributes for screen readers.
findings.root_cause: The button toggles state via React useState but does not expose accessibility attributes to the DOM.
findings.evidence: BlockchainProofCard.jsx:58: <button type='button' onClick={() => setDetailsExpanded((prev) => !prev)} ...>
findings.reproduction: Inspect the button using Chrome DevTools Accessibility pane; it lacks aria-expanded state.
findings.impact: Screen reader users cannot determine whether technical verification details are currently expanded or collapsed.
findings.recommendation: Add aria-expanded={detailsExpanded} and aria-controls='verification-details-panel' to the toggle button.
findings.regression_test: Automated Axe / Lighthouse accessibility audit.

findings.description: MongoDB sensor collection READINGS lacks a Time-To-Live (TTL) index or size cap, risking unbounded disk growth.
findings.root_cause: getMongoContext ensures indexes on deviceId and receivedAt, but does not configure expireAfterSeconds or a capped collection.
findings.evidence: sensorRoutes.js:40-43 creates compound indexes on deviceId, hiveId, and receivedAt, but no TTL index.
findings.reproduction: Inspect MongoDB collection indexes using mongosh; no TTL index exists on receivedAt or timestamp.
findings.impact: High-volume IoT telemetry (1 reading every 3s) will exhaust free-tier MongoDB Atlas storage quotas within weeks.
findings.recommendation: Add a 30-day TTL index: sensorReadingsCollection.createIndex({ receivedAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: 2592000 }).
findings.regression_test: Verify MongoDB collection index includes expireAfterSeconds.
